The best, and very ironic part about this is that it would have required technology that wasn't possible yet to fake the moon landing. no one could film a 2 hour, high frame rate film (Which requires SO many rolls of film in the first place without the high frame rate to slow things down) then develop, edit, and THEN make sure that every single frame was free of dust, hair, and wasn't damaged.
That makes no sense. They could easily have used the same broadcast cameras they used on the actual missions and digital tape storage.

That camera recorded digitally at 11fps (iirc) and was processed to broadcast smoothly at some other frame rate. On top of that, fitting all of that data onto one reel to avoid any cuts in footage playback would require an amazing amount of physical and digital space if it were 1s and 0s, or a reel of film so large it wouldn't be usable. then cover ups with all the manufacturers, actors, designers, and everyone else to make sure no holes were poked, if all the footage was perfect, saved correctly, and didn't mess up while being broadcast.

Could it have happened? possibly. Was it easier to use science to send 3 men to the moon? most likely.

They managed to record the footage on the moon and broadcast/store it on earth. Saying it would have been impossible to hoax because they couldn't have had the camera on a set somewhere is nonsense.

I'm not inclined to think the moon landings were a hoax, but the argument I replied to just made no kind of sense at all.
